items.title: 61529_Maxine Sullivan oral history interview
items.q: when Sarah Vaughan was making recordings with the big arrangements and violins and this had nothing to do with her rendition or her voice, she would wind up working smaller clubs

ctx.x: I would rather not sing with a big orchestra with all the woodwinds and all the strings. I'll tell you why. Because you're heard on recordings or you're heard on radio or television, you know, with the larger orchestra, and then you wind up working in a club where you got a trio or a whatever and the audience expects to hear what they heard on the recording and it's not the same.

If I may say so, when Sarah Vaughan was making recordings with the big arrangements and violins and this had nothing to do with her rendition or her voice, she would wind up working smaller clubs and believe you me, without the large arrangements, it made a difference. It made no difference in her vocal rendition or her voice --
